text: dynamic structure given $$   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{}   +   \boldsymbol{\beta}_{}   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}   +   \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t},   \quad   \mathrm{}   \quad   \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}   \sim   \mathcal{N}   \left(   \mathbf{0},   \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{}   \right) $$ \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}\), \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}\), \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\) random variables, \(\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{}\), \(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{}\), \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{}\) model parameters. , \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}\) vector latent variables time \(t\) individual \(\), \(\boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}\) represents vector latent variables time \(t - 1\) individual \(\), \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\) represents vector dynamic noise time \(t\) individual \(\). \(\boldsymbol{\alpha}_{}\) denotes vector intercepts, \(\boldsymbol{\beta}_{}\) matrix autoregression cross regression coefficients, \(\boldsymbol{\Psi}_{}\) covariance matrix \(\boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t}\). center = TRUE, dynamic structure parameterized follows $$   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\mu}_{}   +   \boldsymbol{\beta}_{}   \left(     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t - 1}     -     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{}   \right)   +   \boldsymbol{\zeta}_{, t} $$ \(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{}\) equilibrium level latent state toward system pulled time.

title: Fit the First-Order Vector Autoregressive Model by ID — FitVARMxID
text: continuous-time parameterization, ct = TRUE, dynamic structure given $$   \mathrm{d}   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   =   \left(   \boldsymbol{\alpha}_{}   +   \boldsymbol{\beta}_{}   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   \right)   \mathrm{d} t   +   \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{}^{\frac{1}{2}}   \mathrm{d}   \mathbf{W}_{, t} $$ note \(\mathrm{d}\boldsymbol{W}\) Wiener process Brownian motion, represents random fluctuations. center = TRUE, dynamic structure parameterized follows $$   \mathrm{d}   \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}   =   \boldsymbol{\beta}_{}   \left(     \boldsymbol{\eta}_{, t}     -     \boldsymbol{\mu}_{}   \right)   \mathrm{d} t   +   \boldsymbol{\Psi}_{}^{\frac{1}{2}}   \mathrm{d}   \mathbf{W}_{, t} $$
